name: LibriSpeech
ability_definition: The ability to identify and understand the speech of another person.

task_realism.reasoning: Transcribing real human speech is a direct test of the 'identify speech' part of the ability. But the speech is read audiobook narration, which is fluent, planned and well-articulated. Workplace speech is mostly spontaneous and conversational, with disfluencies, overlapping talk, interruptions and turn-taking. The core task is authentic, but its instances are an easy, unrepresentative subset.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: The audio is fairly clean, close-mic'd recording. It is pre-segmented into utterances, carries no real-time or interactive demands, and leaves out far-field, noisy, telephone and multi-speaker conditions. Test-other adds some harder speakers and acoustics, but the distribution is still far easier than real settings such as meetings, factories, call centers or field work. The listener also cannot ask for clarification, and wrong words carry no stakes.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It measures only word-level identification. Comprehension is never checked. It is English-only, has limited accent and dialect diversity, and uses one speaking style (read). It omits spontaneous speech, cross-talk, speaker variability under stress, and noise robustness, all of which are central to understanding another person's speech. The 'understand' half of the ability is untested.

format_match.reasoning: Input is real recorded human audio, which is a genuine artifact. Output is normalized text (uppercase, no punctuation) of short segmented utterances scored by WER. Real work needs meaning-preserving understanding or usable transcripts of continuous, unsegmented, multi-party audio, often with punctuation, speaker attribution and a follow-up action.

transferability_reasoning: LibriSpeech tests the identification half of speech recognition directly, using real human audio and a standard WER metric. However, its read, clean, English-only audiobook speech is a narrow and easy slice of workplace speech. It gives no evidence about comprehension, conversational or noisy conditions, or accent diversity, so strong scores transfer only partially to real-world ability to understand another person's speech.

2020.model_or_system: Conformer XXL+ with noisy student training and wav2vec 2.0 pre-training (Zhang et al., Google)
2020.metric: word error rate (%) on LibriSpeech test-other; lower is better
2020.human_reference: General adult listeners and working transcribers: fluent English speakers doing careful verbatim transcription of recorded speech

2021.model_or_system: Conformer XXL with wav2vec 2.0 pre-training and noisy student training (Google Brain, Zhang et al.)
2021.metric: word error rate (%) on LibriSpeech test-clean, lower is better
2021.human_reference: General adult listeners, with typical non-professional human transcribers as the practical comparison. Speech recognition is a general ability used across most jobs.

2022.model_or_system: Conformer XXL+ with wav2vec 2.0 pre-training and noisy student training (Zhang et al., Google)
2022.metric: word error rate (%) on LibriSpeech test-other; lower is better
2022.human_reference: General adult working population: typical fluent listeners who identify and understand the speech of others at work. Proxied by non-expert human transcribers.

2023.model_or_system: Conformer XXL, wav2vec 2.0 pre-trained + noisy student training with SpecAugment (Zhang et al., Google)
2023.metric: word error rate (%) on LibriSpeech test-other (lower is better)
2023.human_reference: English-proficient adults doing careful word-level transcription of read speech (general educated workforce and non-specialist transcribers)
